draft.title: Aldehydes, ketones and carboxylic acids
card: has a C=O group on the end carbon of the chain, so that carbon is also bonded to a hydrogen. Names end in -al, such as ethanal.
has a C=O group on a carbon inside the chain, so that carbon is bonded to two other carbons. Names end in -one, such as propanone.
has a COOH group on the end carbon of the chain. Names end in -oic acid, such as ethanoic acid.
Carboxylic acids are weak acids. They ionise only partly in water, giving a few H+ ions and leaving most molecules unchanged.
draft.remember: C=O in all three: aldehydes and ketones differ by where it sits, and COOH makes a weak acid.

a.why: Propanone has its C=O on the middle carbon, bonded to two other carbons, so it is a ketone. Propanal also has C=O, but it is on the end carbon with a hydrogen, which makes it an aldehyde.
a.clue: Look for C=O on a carbon inside the chain.

b.q: A student tests 0.1 M ethanoic acid and 0.1 M hydrochloric acid. The ethanoic acid has a higher pH. What is the best explanation?
opts: Ethanoic acid ionises only partly in water
Ethanoic acid has fewer carbon atoms than HCl
Ethanoic acid ionises completely in water
Ethanoic acid has no hydrogen that can be lost
b.why: A carboxylic acid is a weak acid, so only some molecules ionise and fewer H+ ions form. That gives a higher pH. Complete ionisation would give a lower pH, as it does for hydrochloric acid.
b.clue: Both solutions have the same concentration, so think about how much ionises.

b.best: Ethanoic acid ionises only partly in water
